turn2.differences: The author's c1-c3 conditions match my own reading of the request condition-for-condition (team, exact title, content mention). The only implicit condition not separately listed is that the target must be a Linear 'document' object rather than another entity type, but this is self-evident since only documents were considered as candidates.

ambiguity_effects.explain: A careful reader naturally takes 'the Growth team's document' to mean a document directly filed under that team (teamId = t-growth), not one merely linked to a project that might belong to the team. d-team-f1 has no teamId and only a projectId, so it fails this condition on a careful reading, even though a careless reader might be swayed by the project's name. This is a near-miss, not a true ambiguity.

A careful reader expects an exact title match. d-title ('Draft note', singular) fails this on close reading, even though a careless reader skimming might treat it as the same title. Since an exact match (d-target) exists, there's no genuine ambiguity here.

In principle 'mentions' could mean literal phrase vs. topical reference, but no candidate record is borderline on this distinction: matching documents use the exact phrase, and the non-matching one (d-content-f0) is on an entirely unrelated topic. So this ambiguity doesn't affect which records match here.

turn2.naturalness_note: The request reads like a plausible, if slightly formal, real-world instruction from someone renaming their own draft document. The only slightly test-like touch is the precise em-dash in the target title ('Referral pilot — launch notes'), which a user might type via copy-paste rather than by hand, but this isn't implausible.
